executiveSummary: GM1709's official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, centre, 38,273 residents, 39 neighbourhoods, eleven BAG places, 30 BRT settlements and ten logical road-border links are internally coherent, and all ten presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Moerdijk is a low-lying delta municipality around the Hollands Diep, Volkerak, Mark/Dintel system and protected polders, with eleven dispersed towns/villages, two rail stations, the A16 Moerdijk crossing, A4/A29, A17/A59, major rail/freight/waterway/pipeline corridors and a nationally important port/industrial cluster. The regional authority distinguishes coastal, river, transition-zone, polder-breach and extreme-rain flood mechanisms. Waterschap Brabantse Delta is planning reinforcement on Willemstad–Noordschans and the 17 km Moerdijk–Drimmelen primary-defence trajectories, but planning status is not event-time failure or safety. The simulator reports a municipality-wide 2.454003 m river depth at both T+24 and T+72, 5,583 rising to 6,440 affected and 375,681 rising to 1,471,188 person-hours without a selected Hollands Diep/Mark/Dintel boundary condition, defence/breach, connected footprint, arrival, velocity or recession. Pluvial T+24 reports 0.551524 m and zero affected while degrading every service and accumulating 184,655 person-hours, without a rain event, terrain, sewer/polder or pump-control state. Direct coastal depth is correctly zero in the inspected canonical fixture and should remain suppressed unless a governed transition-zone event proves connectivity. The more fundamental omission is industrial risk: the current VRMWB Seveso plan lists sixteen high-threshold establishments in Moerdijk or Heijningen across warehouse fire, BLEVE, gas-cloud explosion, flare, pool/tank fire, dispersion, explosion and environmental scenarios, none represented by the ten presets. The CBS Industrieterrein Moerdijk neighbourhood has an official resident population of zero but 390 businesses and 458 non-residential buildings; all inspected scenarios therefore show zero affected there, while Port of Moerdijk reports over 400 businesses and more than 20,000 jobs municipality-wide at the port. Resident exposure is not workforce, visitor, hazardous-site, economic or responder exposure. The public snapshot contains 213 partial water-control/wastewater points, Enexis/Brabant Water/Ziggo responsibility areas, a high-demand grid-planning sample, 126 antenna sites, 29 education locations and three indicative air stations, but no live topology, backup, occupancy or restoration state. No acute hospital lies inside; care access is cross-boundary. Road transfer currently treats six physical families, while rail, shipping and pipelines remain context only; static capacity cannot represent port logistics or evacuation. Public preparedness pages and port 72-hour engagement do not publish a municipality-wide operational support-site, stock or action ledger, so those quantities remain Unknown. Exact hazard, affected, service and recovery values must be suppressed or labelled synthetic until governed event geometry, dynamic occupancy and confirmed first-72-hour actions exist; zeros and NoData must never become proof of absence, safety, accessibility or recovery.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1709 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM1709 as Moerdijk in Noord-Brabant and Veiligheidsregio Midden- en West-Brabant, with 38,273 residents, density 240/km², 23.5% aged 65 or older and 5,382 one-person households. The reference point [4.543280198714641,51.652932330237164] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Thirty-nine neighbourhoods in eleven districts sum to 38,255 residents, eighteen below the municipal control (-0.047%); published households total 17,070 and rounded age-65-plus rows 8,975. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 38,273 without rewriting observations.

Eleven BAG places have no retained centre outside the generalized boundary. Thirty BRT features comprise six buurtschappen, two deelkernen, seven gehuchten and fifteen woonkernen; labels and descriptive populations are not independent municipal controls.

Industrieterrein Moerdijk's published resident population is zero, while its row retains 390 businesses, 458 non-residential buildings and 1,878 hectares of land. The exact resident zero must remain zero, but it does not mean nobody is present or no operational exposure exists.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2027 flood, vital-infrastructure and transport mechanisms
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2027, current authority publication inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The authority distinguishes flooding from sea, high river levels, polder filling/dike breach and extreme weather. In the Benedenrivierengebied it separately defines coast, Rhine/Meuse river and central transition-zone scenarios driven by storm surge, river discharge and storm-surge-barrier closure strategy.

The region borders the Hollands Diep and contains Dintel/Markvliet flood pathways; the authority gives a Maas high-water travel time to Moerdijk of about 3.5–4 days and warns that a breach can cascade into vital-infrastructure failure or an adjacent dike ring. These are scenario mechanics, not a selected breach or municipal depth.

The Brabantroute and line 12 carry passengers, freight and dangerous goods through Moerdijk/Zevenbergen/Lage Zwaluwe, with dangerous-goods yards at Lage Zwaluwe and Moerdijk. The sea port sits on Hollands Diep; shipping incidents can cause fire, explosion, pollution or obstruction.

A major pipeline corridor between Rotterdam and Antwerp branches to Moerdijk/Vlissingen and carries pressurized flammable/toxic products. Regional risk context does not disclose operational topology, shipment, line-pack, isolation or current state.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Generiek Rampbestrijdingsplan Seveso-inrichtingen version 7.0
evidenceSources.edition: Version 7.0, established 4 July 2024, stated expiry 2027; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The operational plan applies to high-threshold Seveso establishments and defines eight external-effect scenarios: warehouse fire, BLEVE, gas-cloud explosion, flare fire, pool/tank fire, dispersion, explosion and environmental contamination.

The versioned table lists sixteen establishments located in Moerdijk or Heijningen, including Shell, Basell, Stolthaven, Coatex, dangerous-goods logistics/storage and chemical businesses. It is a July 2024 planning inventory, not proof of audit-time process, inventory or incident state.

The plan requires source/effect-zone control, evacuation or shelter decisions, vulnerable-person identification, meteo/source-strength-based effect areas, access preservation and communication with care, utilities, RWS, water board, RIVM, port and neighbouring regions.

It explicitly covers contaminated extinguishing water reaching surface water, sewers and RWZI, possible temporary pump shutdown, ship-traffic restrictions and sustained responder food/fuel logistics. None of these causal branches exists in the ten simulator presets.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Current port scale, multimodal role and operational preparedness context
evidenceSources.edition: Current operator pages and 2025–2030 safety programme inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The port reports over 400 businesses and more than 20,000 jobs and identifies itself as a national sea port and multimodal cluster for chemistry, energy, recycling, road, rail, inland/short-sea shipping and pipelines. Jobs are not a simultaneous occupancy observation.

The operator reports a 24/7 professional industrial fire service with a six-minute response target, a 24/7 staffed communication centre and port alerting. These are provider-stated capabilities/targets, not guaranteed availability, incident arrival or municipal fire capacity.

The main A17 entrance and internal LPM road are described as always open except during incidents; other gates have schedules. This is ordinary operating context and explicitly preserves a calamity exception, not a scenario-time open-state guarantee.

The port and municipality report discussing business emergency plans and the first 72 hours, while the 2025–2030 safety programme addresses physical, cyber/hybrid, climate and energy-transition risks. Engagement and plans do not disclose stocks, backup endurance, mutual-aid availability or completed actions.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Primary-defence projects and public flood preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Current project and safe-dikes pages inspected 3 September 2026; Moerdijk–Drimmelen 2024–2031 plan-development phase; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The 17 km Moerdijk–Drimmelen primary defence protects against high water; parts do not meet future standards, a preferred decision was established in November 2025 and implementation is expected from 2028. The water board says this does not mean the defence is currently unsafe.

A separate Willemstad–Noordschans primary defence protects against Hollands Diep high water and has a 2026 concept preferred alternative. Current and planned reinforcement status is not event-time overtopping, breach probability or performance.

The municipality warns that some areas' relation to water and more extreme weather increase flood concern and publishes household guidance for flood, severe weather and utility loss. Guidance is not a warning, forecast, flood surface or evacuation order.
No inspected current municipal source publishes a governed emergency-support-point catalogue, site count, staffing, stock or opening state. This remains Unknown rather than an inferred zero.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Partial IMWA water-control and DAMO wastewater registers
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z; CC BY-SA 4.0; publisher-variable completeness
supports: Full-resolution polygon containment assigns 213 register points to GM1709: 165 weirs, 31 surface-water pumps, thirteen sewer pumps, three sluices and RWZI Willemstad.

Only 38 points have a non-null capacity field and 175 do not. Remaining values do not establish comparable units, connected catchments, flow direction, control modes, energy/backup, storage, maintenance, crew or incident state.

All 213 records carry register status 'gerealiseerd'. This is publisher register status at retrieval, not evidence that each asset is operating, powered, available or correctly controlled at scenario time.
Point presence is context only and partial coverage never proves that unlisted assets are absent. No point may alter Water or Drainage without a governed event binding and valid-time state.

evidenceSources.edition: NWB-light 2026-08-01 and transport snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03, CC0; OVapi schedule 2026-08-30 through 2026-12-12; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 2026-07-03, CC0
supports: Ten logical road links connect seven neighbours through six physical families: three A16 records share NWB-road-16, A4/A29 share NWB-road-4 and A59/N59 share NWB-road-59. Repeated records are non-additive series links.

Distances 0.100–3.968 km and nominal 150/260 values are boundary geometry and scenario-unit ceilings, not lanes, vehicles/hour, bridge capacity, evacuation throughput or travel time. Moerdijkbrug/Hollands Diep crossing failure is not separately typed.

Zevenbergen and Lage Zwaluwe stations lie inside GM1709 and 91 GTFS stop areas are retained. Geometry/schedule do not establish live rail/bus, freight, dangerous-goods-yard, accessible vehicle, staff, fuel or evacuation state. The municipal Beukenlaan bridge page reports a current all-traffic closure, showing local state can differ from the static border graph.

No acute hospital lies inside GM1709. RIVM annual records place Bravis Roosendaal about 15.6 km, Albert Schweitzer Dordrecht 18.2 km and Amphia Breda 19.2 km straight-line from the municipal reference point; offers and distance do not prove route, acceptance, staffing or surge.

evidenceSources.edition: Deployment/public queries retrieved 2–3 September 2026; licences and cadence remain source-specific

Public Domain territories are responsibility context, not topology, coverage quality, service or restoration.

One postcode sample 4791AM maps to Enexis area MDK Moerdijk and reports planning fields: withdrawal existing 344.8 MW, required 201.4 MW, queue 155.4 MW/115 requests; injection existing 349.9 MW, required 163.8 MW, queue 105.4 MW/79 requests; nineteen projects, earliest 2026. Three RIVM network points reported indicative PM2.5 at 17:00 UTC on 2 September 2026; these are ambient point observations, not a chemical-release plume, exposure map or forecast. The deployment assigns zero local NDW situations, KNMI weather stations, Waterinfo observations/forecasts and 365-day seismic origins; no-match is NoData, never normal, open, dry or safe.
